title: Creators Wait 40 Minutes for Rs 709 Himachali Feast in Delhi
excerpt: At the Himachal Bhawan canteen near Mandi House, duo Bhawna and Nitin worked through Siddu, a loaded Veg Himachali Thali and chicken masala — and the total bill was Rs 709.
body:
• Creator duo Bhawna and Nitin waited 40 minutes at the Himachal Pradesh State Bhawan Canteen in Delhi before ordering a spread of Pahadi dishes.
  • Their order — Siddu, a Veg Himachali Thali and chicken masala — came to a total bill of Rs 709.
  • The thali alone packed in more than a dozen items, from Meetha Bhat and Sepu Vadi to Rajmah Madra, Taliya Mash and Chambyali Palda.
  • The canteen sits at Himachal Bhawan, 27 Sikandra Road near Mandi House, and serves breakfast, lunch and dinner.

NEW DELHI — For anyone chasing Pahadi flavours without leaving the capital, the Himachal Pradesh State Bhawan Canteen in Delhi is drawing a fresh round of attention after a food video by creator duo Bhawna and Nitin worked its way through a full Himachali spread. The pair took a food trail through the canteen to discover the flavours of Himachal Pradesh in the heart of the capital — and it began with a wait. After 40 minutes of waiting, the duo finally ordered a variety of Pahadi delicacies. "Trust me, it is worth the wait," one of them shared before showing what they ate.

They started with a traditional Siddu, served with desi ghee and walnut chutney. "This is the first time I had such an authentic Siddu in Delhi," the creator shared. That verdict lines up with how the canteen is described in guides to Delhi's State Bhawan canteens: Restaurant India calls the small Himachal Bhawan canteen loved for its Pahadi-style food, with dishes that are light, mildly spiced and prepared with traditional techniques, and lists Siddu — a local bread served with ghee and chutney — as a must-try, alongside Himachali Rajma Chawal and Chana Madra.

The centrepiece was a traditional Veg Himachali Thali, which included different types of sabzi, roti and rice. The full line-up was Meetha Bhat, Sepu Vadi, Missi Roti, Rajmah Madra, Taliya Mash, Chambyali Palda, Kabuli Chana Dal, Moong Dal, Matar Paneer, kheeru, Raita (khata-meetha), plain tandoori roti and plain rice. "All the dishes had an authentic Himachali taste. If you like Pahadi cuisine, this thali is a must-try," the creator added. The pair also ordered a plate of chicken masala, which they described as soft and juicy. Their total bill for the whole order came to Rs 709.

The canteen is at Himachal Bhawan, 27 Sikandra Road near the Mandi House metro station, where HerZindagi's Mandi House food guide likewise recommends the Himachali Thali, naming Chana Madra and Sepu Vadi as the dishes to try, and notes that the canteen offers an authentic taste of Himachali cuisine at reasonable prices. That fits the wider State Bhawan pattern in Delhi: the canteens, set inside state guest houses, are known for simple, honest regional food at affordable prices, and are popular with office workers, students and food enthusiasts.

Planning a visit around the video? The Himachal Bhawan Canteen serves breakfast from 8 am to 10 am, lunch from 1 pm to 3 pm and dinner from 8 pm to 10 pm. Beyond what the duo ordered, the menu includes a Non-Veg Himachali Thali, Chha Meat, Chicken Anardana and Bathu Ke Kheer, along with Sepu Vadi, Chana Madra, Kheru, Badana Meetha and Siddu. A word of honest balance: not every Himachali diner has been as generous as the creators. Writing in Hill Post after a visit to the same Mandi House canteen, a Himachali writer found the thali a letdown and praised only the Meetha Bhaat — a reminder that a 40-minute queue buys you a debated feast, not a unanimous one. On the creators' telling, though, Rs 709 for Siddu, a loaded thali and chicken masala is a hill feast at plains prices.
nri_angle: For diaspora readers who miss hill food, Delhi's State Bhawan canteens — and videos like this one — map where a full regional thali from back home can still be found away from home.
author: Diaspora Desk
